insight: Both Matthew 5:16 and 1 Peter 2:12 emphasize the importance of believers' good works as a visible testimony before non-believers. Matthew highlights that believers' light should shine publicly so that onlookers glorify God, while Peter focuses on maintaining honorable conduct among Gentiles to silence slander and lead observers to glorify God at His visitation. In both passages, the good works are not for self-glorification but serve to direct glory to God through transformed lives witnessed by others.
